solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Combustible matter gathered up for range

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood built to be burned, often for a funeral

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to have gathered something is to have understood or seen it

explanation.surface: Fuel collected together for a cooking stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a kitchen stove beside the combustible matter, but it is a mountain range. 'Up' turns SEEN into NEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are a mountain range between France and Spain, so a proper-name example of a range.

clue.text: I'll put up there again

parts.note: the I of I'll is taken as the letter I, the will being left as a link
to put up money at an auction is to bid

explanation.surface: Someone offering to host a guest once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' suggests giving someone a bed; here it means offering a price.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in footnotes means 'in the same place', i.e. the reference cited there again.

clue.text: Piece of corn cob for starter, followed by fruit (skipping second part of meal)

indicators.note: the first letter of cob is used as the opening piece of the answer
skipping means leaving out a letter from the fruit

parts.note: the lichee (also lychee) is a sweet Chinese fruit

indicators.note: the second letter of the word meal is the part removed

explanation.surface: A lunch menu: corn on the cob as a starter, then fruit, missing out the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second part of meal' looks like the main course but is just the letter E, which 'skipping' drops from LICHEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is trite, overused material, so a hackneyed saying is a piece of corn.

clue.text: Set the pace after winning round, but dropped slowly down

indicators.note: after places the pace-setting word behind the winning round

parts.note: in card games a trick is one round of play that a player wins
whoever sets the pace has led

explanation.surface: A runner set the pace after taking a round, but then sank back down the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that moved slowly downward in a thin stream has seeped down drop by drop.

clue.text: Posh tart generally won't have one

definitions.meaning: posh people are the social elite
a tart is open-topped, unlike a pie with its pastry lid on top

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that a hussy is never classy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a loose woman, the snob's target; it is the pastry dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocracy are the top layer of society, and a pie's lid is its top layer of pastry.

clue.text: Depressed censor making revelation?

parts.note: something depressed has been pushed low
to censor a film is to cut it

explanation.surface: A gloomy censor who nonetheless lets something revealing through.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress with a plunging neckline shows a lot, so it reveals more than usual.

clue.text: Representative limbo dancing in Seychelles clubs

indicators.note: in places the shuffled dance inside the island code and the suit letter

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of limbo moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A night of limbo dancing in the clubs of the Seychelles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges the dance's name to MBOLI; 'clubs' here is the card suit, not nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or represents something else.

clue.text: Titbit made from preserve one found at chimps' tea party

parts.note: to preserve food is to can it

parts.words: one found at chimps' tea party
parts.note: a chimpanzee is an ape, and chimps' tea parties were famous zoo and TV advert entertainment in Britain

explanation.surface: A snack made with jam, served at a chimpanzees' tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: PG Tips tea adverts long featured chimps having a tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury morsel served with drinks, a dainty titbit.

clue.text: Sounding increasingly engrossed in hobby?

indicators.note: sounding says the comparative is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: more rapt, a made-up comparative of rapt meaning engrossed

explanation.surface: Someone getting ever more absorbed in their pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hobby' looks like a pastime but is a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby is a small falcon, an example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Action being withdrawn will have no effect

indicators.text: being withdrawn will have no effect
indicators.note: withdrawn suggests drawing the word back to front, and having no effect says it stays unchanged that way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Withdrawing a lawsuit will make no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's word reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an act or action.

clue.text: Morality against biology?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
biology is one example of a science, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: An ethics-versus-biology debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner sense of right and wrong is a person's moral faculty.

clue.text: To scrap democratic right could be to give up entirely

parts.note: the prefix de- signals removing or undoing something
the vote is the fundamental right in a democracy

explanation.surface: Abolishing the franchise might mean surrendering everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun splits the answer as DE-VOTE: taking the vote away.
explanation.definitionFit: To give oneself or one's time wholly to something is to dedicate it entirely.

clue.text: Attach no weight to newspaper chart showing who's most powerful

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group, such as a party newspaper
O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Telling a newspaper to give no weight to a chart of the powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: This diagram maps an organisation's structure, showing who reports to whom and who sits at the top.

clue.text: Rank animals and men by measure of length?

indicators.note: by places the men right next to the measure

parts.note: a pole is an old unit of length, five and a half yards
cats is slang for men or guys, as in jazz cats

explanation.surface: Ranking animals and people by height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a verb meaning sort; here it is an adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Polecats are notoriously smelly creatures of the weasel family, so rank animals.

clue.text: X American troops retreating in ring

indicators.note: retreating sends both the number and the soldiers backwards

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: US forces pulling back inside a cordon marked X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreating' reverses TENGIS to give the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a seal set into a finger ring, giving the signet ring.

clue.text: Denounce boss's pay scale

parts.note: an exec, short for executive, is a boss
a rate is a scale of pay

explanation.surface: Condemning the size of the chief executive's salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn something loudly and with loathing.

clue.text: Regulator will do so to make commercial fair

parts.note: an ad is a TV commercial
just means fair or impartial

explanation.surface: An industry watchdog ensuring advertising is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulators correct, tune or bring things into line, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Main route reportedly eroded, cut off

indicators.note: reportedly says the road word is heard, not seen spelt

parts.note: a trunk road is a main road
something eroded has been eaten away, so ate

explanation.surface: A main road that has worn away and been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk road in Britain is a major A-road.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something by chopping off its end is to cut it short.

clue.text: Grounds for some to say: 'Don't go, darling'

indicators.note: some accents pronounce the plea so it is heard as the plural of a sports ground

parts.note: a plea to stay, dear

explanation.surface: A lover pleading with a partner not to leave, as grounds for staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons but means sports arenas.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is the Latinate plural of stadium, a sports ground.

clue.text: Superficial check on the most impoverished?

definitions.meaning: an allergy test on the surface of the body
skint is British slang for broke, so its jokey superlative means poorest

explanation.surface: A cursory inspection of the poorest people.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy test done on the surface of the body is literally superficial; skint is British slang for penniless.

clue.text: Dub remix of 'The King' lacking energy

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so these letters are reordered
lacking says a letter is missing from the rearranged pool

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A new dub mix of an Elvis track, lacking its usual energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dub' and 'remix' suggest reggae music; Dub is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to confer a title by touching the shoulders with a sword.

clue.text: Film director's 'igh and mighty attitude

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows a dropped aitch, so the same letter goes from the attitude word

parts.note: haughty arrogance, the high and mighty manner

explanation.surface: A film director's lofty arrogance, mocked in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'igh, with its missing H, tells you to drop that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An auteur is a director whose personal vision dominates their films; the 's here is 'is'.

clue.text: Made up where mountains might be found round here?

definitions.meaning: made amends or compensated for a wrong

definitions.text: where mountains might be found round here?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., this points to the grid's 1 Down, where the range sits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Round here' means in this very puzzle: the mountain range is the entry at one down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has made up for a wrong has made amends and compensated for it.

clue.text: Was Spice Girl playing old wooden instrument?

parts.note: did stands in for was, as in 'Was it? Yes, it did'
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice
to do a part is to play it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Spice Girl was performing on an antique wooden instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is an Aboriginal Australian wind instrument made from a hollowed branch.

clue.text: Fluid-filled tube — what Yorkshire cows chew over?

indicators.note: chew over hints at turning the dialect phrase back to front

parts.note: cows chew the cud, which in Yorkshire dialect is t' cud

explanation.surface: A cow's digestive tract and the cud it ruminates on.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech shortens 'the' to t'. 'Over' reverses TCUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a vessel in the body carrying fluid, such as a tear duct.

clue.text: Doubly possessive French chap

parts.note: du and de both mean 'of' in French, the possessive
du and de both mean 'of' in French, the possessive

explanation.surface: A greedy Frenchman, twice as possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is American slang for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Cross Basil won't mention it — forgetting finally one time

indicators.note: forgetting means a letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: Basil Fawlty's famous line in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers is 'Don't mention the war'

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of one

explanation.surface: An angry Basil refusing to raise a subject, forgetting something once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, describing Basil, but is a verb meaning foil.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone's plans is to block or frustrate them.

clue.text: Story encrypted by neat code

indicators.note: encrypting scrambles text, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale hidden in a tidy cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing tale about a real incident.
